subject: Horizon Analytics: CAIQ extract, subprocessor residency table & pen-test request
body:
From: Sam Perez <sam.perez@horizon-analytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Monica Ruiz <mruiz@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ extract + subprocessor residency table & pen-test request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As part of our vendor onboarding checklist in Security & Procurement we need a couple of items before we can finalize a PO:

1) A CAIQ-style extract that maps Redwood controls to our control set (high level is fine, we only need control IDs and short notes).
2) A subprocessor roster with residency flags (US / EU / APAC) and any data-in-transit encryption notes for each entry.
3) Confirm whether Horizon can run a timeboxed penetration test against a staging environment (non-production, read-only data, IP allowlist). If yes, we need the process and an SLA for scheduling.

Do you have a standard deliverable for (1) and (2)? If there are existing artifacts you can share we can accelerate our review. Also please include an intended timeline — we are targeting a PO by end of month.

Appreciate it —
Sam Perez
Security Operations Lead
Horizon Analytics

---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sam Perez <sam.perez@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ extract + subprocessor residency table & pen-test request

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list.

We can provide a CAIQ extract and a subprocessor residency table. I attached a CSV with our current roster and a draft CAIQ extract PDF for your review (redacted where appropriate).

On pen-testing: we do permit scheduled third-party security assessments against a dedicated staging environment. A few important notes up-front:
- We require a signed NDA and an authorized scoping doc.
- Tests must be limited to non-production environments; no data exfiltration, no social-engineering tests.
- Testing windows are scheduled 10 business days after scoping approval.
- Any findings are triaged under our vulnerability disclosure process; critical issues will trigger immediate mitigation.

Ben — can you confirm SOC 2 availability and whether we should include a short attestation about ephemeral key rotation and KV cache access controls in the CAIQ extract?

Naomi — looping you for DPA / contract redlines that Horizon may request (they mentioned timeline pressure).

Action items:
- I: Provide initial artifacts (attached) and HubSpot deal link.
- Ben: Confirm SOC 2 and pen-test logistics.
- Naomi: Confirm DPA point-of-contact and if procurement approval flow needs escalation.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_residency_20260412.csv, redwood_caiq_control_extract_20260412.pdf

On Mon, Apr 12, 2026 at 11:45 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com> wrote:

> Hi all — quick updates in-line.
>
> Thanks Sam — we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report (we’ve attached the latest redacted PDF). The CAIQ extract included by Irene intentionally omits secret material (API keys, ephemeral credentials). For control notes on ephemeral key rotation and KV cache access I’d add:
> - Ephemeral key rotation: 15-minute TTL for short-lived session credentials used in hosted API; auditable rotation logs retained 90 days.
> - KV cache access: role-based access control enforced; service account separation between runtime and telemetry; only hashed references stored in telemetry exports.
>
> Pen-test: we support third-party assessments under our standard pen-test agreement (attached sample). Key constraints:
> 1) Testable staging environment will be available between 8a-6p PT M-F; we require an allowlist of source IPs at least 72 hours before the window.
> 2) No automated denial-of-service-style testing without prior written approval.
> 3) We ask for a 30-day remediation schedule for any P1/P2 items; we can accelerate critical fixes if necessary.
>
> I’ll coordinate with Infra to provision a dedicated staging sandbox and share an access checklist.
>
> Ben Carter
> Director, Security & Compliance
> Redwood Inference
>
> Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf, THIRDPARTY-PENTEST-AGREEMENT-sample.pdf


On Thu, Apr 15, 2026 at 14:02:00 -07:00 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com> wrote:

Hi Sam — thanks for the prompt.

From a contracts side we can:
- Accept Horizon’s standard PO and sign Redwood’s DPA with one commercial redline (we’ll send the proposed clause on residency limits).
- We’ll require procurement contact and a certificate of insurance if Horizon intends to run an active test.

Sam — can you confirm the procurement email and the preferred test window (week of Apr 26 or May 10)? We’ll hold the staging sandbox slot pending scoping doc and PO.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
VP, Legal & Privacy
Redwood Inference
